searches.formulation:
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $\lambda,\mu,
u$ be partitions with at most $n$ parts, $|\lambda|+|\mu|=|
u|$ and Littlewood-Richardson coefficient $c^{
u}_{\lambda\mu}>0$. Let $H=H(\lambda,\mu,
u)\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}$, $D= inom{n-1}{2}$, be the hive polytope of Knutson and Tao: the set of real labellings of the $D$ interior vertices of the triangular hive array of side $n$ whose border labels are $0$ at the apex and the partial sums of $\lambda$, $\mu$ and $
u$ along the three sides, and which satisfy every rhombus inequality (the sum of the labels at the two obtuse vertices of each unit rhombus is at least the sum at the two acute vertices). $H$ is a rational polytope whose lattice points are the integral hives, so that $\#(tH\cap\mathbb{Z}^{D})=c^{t
u}_{t\lambda,t\mu}$ for every integer $t\ge 1$.

Statement. For every such triple, $H(\lambda,\mu,
u)$ is $\mathrm{GL}_{D}(\mathbb{Z})$-equidecomposable with a lattice polytope: there exist finitely many relatively open rational simplices $T_{1},\dots,T_{r}$ with $H= igsqcup_{i=1}^{r}T_{i}$ (disjoint union, every face of the decomposition counted once as the relative interior of a simplex of some dimension between $0$ and $\dim H$) and affine unimodular maps $U_{i}(x)=A_{i}x+b_{i}$ with $A_{i}\in\mathrm{GL}_{D}(\mathbb{Z})$ and $b_{i}\in\mathbb{Z}^{D}$, such that the images $U_{1}(T_{1}),\dots,U_{r}(T_{r})$ are pairwise disjoint and $Q= igsqcup_{i=1}^{r}U_{i}(T_{i})$ is a lattice polytope, that is, a convex polytope all of whose vertices lie in $\mathbb{Z}^{D}$. In particular $\#(tH\cap\mathbb{Z}^{D})=\#(tQ\cap\mathbb{Z}^{D})$ for every $t\ge 1$, so the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial $c^{t
u}_{t\lambda,t\mu}$ is the Ehrhart polynomial of the lattice polytope $Q$.

reason: Across the exact statement and all three declared neighbours, no source poses or settles the equidecomposability of hive polytopes with a lattice polytope, and the fully read sources locate the question precisely at the frontier. Haase and McAllister (0709.4070v1, read in full) name the Littlewood-Richardson polynomials of Derksen-Weyman among the motivating cases of period collapse whose known proofs are not polyhedral, state Conjecture 3.2 (equidecomposability with a disjoint union of integral open simplices) and Question 4.1 as open, and show by Example 2.4 that the single-lattice-polytope form fails for general rational polytopes, so the hive case needs the special structure of the family; their Proposition 4.3 yields only weak equidecomposability with rational translations. Erbe-Haase-Santos (1807.09485v1, read in full) settle Question 4.1 only for lattice 3-polytopes and show by Example 4 and Remark 5 that the question fails for rational polytopes already in dimension one, so their theorem does not reach hive polytopes, which are rational with vertices of denominator 2 from five parts on (Buch, math/9810180v1, Example 2, read in full). Turner-Wu (1412.0196v1, read in full) separate Ehrhart equivalence from finite rational equidecomposability for polygons, confirming that the Ehrhart form is strictly weaker and that no known invariant settles the hive case. Thawinrak (2211.06810v2, read in full) proves polynomiality algebraically and produces no lattice polytope; Ferudun (2607.22301v2, read in full) uses only the integral dilate qH (Lemma 8, a weak equidecomposability) and proves monomial positivity for at most five parts without any lattice realization; Ghodsi (2609.14357v1, read in full) proves finite-box monomial positivity by exact Ehrhart computation and makes no statement about the h*-vector, period collapse or the geometry of hive polytopes. For the rank restriction, Buch's statement that all corners are integral for n<=4 appears without a printed proof and no printed proof was found, and no work treats n>=5. The weaker Ehrhart form is also unsettled: no source exhibits a lattice polytope Ehrhart-equivalent to a hive polytope with non-integral vertices, and none refutes it (for instance by a negative h*-coefficient). findings.assumptions: Standard inputs taken from fully read sources: the hive theorem (Buch, Theorem 1, with Fulton's bijection), rationality of hive polytopes with non-integral vertices from five parts on (Buch, Example 2) and Buch's unproved remark that for n<=4 all corners are integral; polynomiality of the stretched coefficient (Derksen-Weyman, Rassart; third proof by Thawinrak, Theorem 1.1), which is period collapse in the Haase-McAllister sense; the definition of GL_n(Z)-equidecomposability (Haase-McAllister, Definition 3.1; Erbe-Haase-Santos, Definition 3). The candidate's assertion that the n<=3 cases are a point or a lattice segment is an elementary observation stated without an accepted source; it does not affect openness for n>=4. No positivity conjecture, no computational sweep and no unverified claim of the Ghodsi or Ferudun papers is used as a premise of the openness finding.

findings.scope: The finding concerns the exact statement as written and its three declared neighbours: the weaker Ehrhart form (some lattice polytope Q with #(tQ cap Z^{dim Q}) = c^{t nu}_{t lambda,t mu}), the weaker Haase-McAllister form (equidecomposability with a disjoint union of integral open simplices, Conjecture 3.2 restricted to hives) and the rank restriction to at most n parts. Both weaker forms are correctly recorded as implied by the statement (equidecomposability preserves dilated lattice-point counts; a lattice polytope is a disjoint union of relatively open lattice simplices). The resolution criteria correctly exclude n<=3 and identify that Buch's n=4 integrality remark, if proved, settles that rank. The openness finding says nothing about the truth of the statement, about the King-Tollu-Toumazet positivity conjecture beyond what the read sources establish, or about Gelfand-Tsetlin analogues.
findings.statement: Statement-4 (candidate-hive-equidecomposable, recorded revision 548): for every n>=2 and every triple of partitions (lambda,mu,nu) with at most n parts, |lambda|+|mu|=|nu| and c^nu_{lambda mu}>0, the Knutson-Tao hive polytope H(lambda,mu,nu) in R^D, D=binom(n-1,2), is GL_D(Z)-equidecomposable with a lattice polytope Q: finitely many relatively open rational simplices T_i partition H, affine unimodular maps U_i(x)=A_i x+b_i with A_i in GL_D(Z), b_i in Z^D carry them to pairwise disjoint pieces whose union Q is a convex polytope with vertices in Z^D; consequently c^{t nu}_{t lambda,t mu} is the Ehrhart polynomial of Q. The count of interior hive vertices binom(n-1,2) and the identification of lattice points with integral hives agree with the supplied Buch exposition (Theorem 1) and with the hive coordinates in the Ghodsi and Ferudun texts. The claim under review is that this statement is open; the recorded claim_digest binds the complete statement, its quantifiers (every triple, finitely many pieces, integral translations), and its declared neighbours.
